title: Health in depth
goal: Describe your symptoms precisely, say how long you've had them, mention allergies and past operations, book a doctor and a test, and understand exactly how to take your medicine.
intro:
In unit 9 you learned to say 'my head hurts'. Now you'll be able to have a real conversation with a doctor or pharmacist: dizziness, nausea, itching, swelling, allergies, blood pressure, tests and injections — and, above all, **how long**: درې ورځې **کېږي** چې ټوخی لرم 'I've had a cough for three days', **له پرون راهيسې** 'since yesterday'.

You'll also learn to follow instructions exactly: **ورځ کې دوه ځله** 'twice a day', **له ډوډۍ وروسته** 'after food', **په خالي ګېډه** 'on an empty stomach' — and why a doctor says وخورئ for one dose but هره ورځ يې خورئ for a course of tablets.

grammar.title: How long? 'I've had it for three days'
grammar.body:
English says 'I **have been** coughing for three days'. Pashto keeps the verb in the **present** — the cough is still going on — and uses one of two patterns:

**1. [length of time] + کېږي چې + present**: درې ورځې **کېږي** چې ټوخی **لرم** 'I've had a cough for three days' (lit. it is becoming three days that I have a cough). Ask: **څو ورځې کېږي چې …؟** 'how many days have you …?'

**2. له [starting point] راهيسې + present** 'since': **له پرون راهيسې** تبه لرم 'I've had a fever since yesterday'. The word after له goes into the oblique: له جمعې راهيسې 'since Friday', له سهاره راهيسې 'since this morning', له دوو اوونيو راهيسې 'for (lit. since) two weeks'. Ask: **له کله راهيسې؟** 'since when?'

**Ago** is **مخکې** after the time, with a past verb: دوه ورځې **مخکې** ناروغ شوم 'I fell ill two days ago'.

**A finished stretch** of time needs no word for 'for' at all: درې ورځې په روغتون کې **وم** 'I was in hospital for three days'.

**The trap**: if it's still happening, don't use a past tense. درې ورځې ټوخی مې **درلود** means 'I had a cough for three days' — and it's over. For a cough you still have, say … ټوخی **لرم**.

grammar.title: Instructions: how often, before or after, and which aspect
grammar.body:
Doctors, pharmacists and medicine labels give instructions in the **polite imperative** (the تاسو-form); to a child or a friend the same words come in the ته-form.

**How often**: ورځ کې **درې ځله** 'three times a day' · **هر اته ساعته** 'every eight hours' · **سهار او ماښام** 'morning and evening' · **يوه يوه** ګولۍ 'one tablet each time' — doubling a number means 'each'.

**When**: **له ډوډۍ وروسته** 'after food' · **له ډوډۍ مخکې** 'before food' · **په خالي ګېډه** 'on an empty stomach' · **له خوب مخکې** 'before bed'. In speech you'll also hear د ډوډۍ نه وروسته.

**For how long**: پنځه ورځې 'for five days' · **تر هغه چې** ګولۍ خلاصې شي 'until the tablets are finished'.

**Which aspect?** For one action, the **perfective**: اوس يوه ګولۍ **وخورئ** 'take one tablet now' — and this is also the usual form on a prescription. When the doctor stresses an ongoing **routine** ('keep taking it'), you'll hear the **imperfective**: هره ورځ يې **خورئ** 'take it every day'. And 'don't' is always **مه + imperfective**: په خالي ګېډه يې **مه خورئ**.

The word يې 'it, them' (a clitic) refers back to the medicine: **يې** وخورئ 'take it'.

culture:
Many people go straight to the **pharmacy** (درملتون) rather than a doctor: pharmacists listen to your symptoms, suggest medicine and in many places will even give an injection. Private clinics cluster in medical streets — in Peshawar, Dabgari Gardens is lined with doctors' signs — and you usually take a number and wait for your **نوبت**. Prescriptions tend to be long; injections and drips (سېروم) are popular, and patients often ask for them.

Illness is a family affair: relatives come along to appointments and stay at the hospital bedside. **Visiting the sick** (د ناروغ پوښتنه) is a social duty — bring fruit, juice or biscuits, keep the visit short, and say **خدای دې شفا درکړي** and **ژر جوړ شې**. You'll also meet the traditional idea of 'hot' and 'cold' foods (ګرم / سوړ خواړه): grandmothers will tell you to avoid 'cold' yoghurt with a cough and eat 'hot' foods like honey and dried fruit in winter.

With a doctor, use تاسو and **ډاکټر صاحب** (to a woman doctor, ډاکټرې صاحبې is common). Patients are often addressed politely too, especially older ones. Women usually prefer a woman doctor, and it's normal to ask for one.

tip.title: Saying exactly what's wrong
tip.body:
- Body part + **مې** + verb, as in unit 9: لاس **مې** خارښت کوي 'my hand itches'.
- Two idioms: **سر مې ګرځي** 'I'm dizzy', **زړه مې بدېږي** 'I feel sick'.
- Swollen = the perfect: پښه مې **پړسېدلې ده** (f), لاس مې **پړسېدلی دی** (m).
- To a doctor: **ډاکټر صاحب** and تاسو.

lessons.title: Since when?

tip.title: … کېږي چې / له … راهيسې
tip.body:
- Still going on? Keep the verb in the **present**.
- **[time] کېږي چې** + present: درې ورځې کېږي چې ټوخی **لرم**.
- **له [start] راهيسې** + present: له جمعې راهيسې تبه **لرم**.
- **Ago** = time + **مخکې** + past: دوه ورځې مخکې ناروغ **شوم**.

tip.title: Telling the doctor about yourself
tip.body:
- Allergies: **له … (څخه) حساسيت لرم** 'I'm allergic to …'.
- Past: **دوه کاله مخکې مې عمليات وشول** 'I had an operation two years ago'.
- Ongoing: **فشار لرم** 'I have high blood pressure'.
- Injections: **پېچکاري وهل** 'to give an injection'.

sentences.native: يوه اوونۍ مخکې ستونی مې خوږېده، اوس ښه دی.
sentences.roman: yáwa owənə́y mə́xke stúnay me xwaẓedə́, os ṣə day.
sentences.en: A week ago my throat was sore, now it's fine.

sentences.native: يوه مياشت مخکې روغتون کې وم.
sentences.roman: yáwa miyā́sht mə́xke roġtún ke wəm.
sentences.en: I was in hospital a month ago.

lessons.title: Taking your medicine

tip.title: How and when to take it
tip.body:
- How often: **ورځ کې دوه ځله**, **هر اته ساعته**, **يوه يوه** ګولۍ 'one each time'.
- When: **له ډوډۍ وروسته / مخکې**, **په خالي ګېډه**, **له خوب مخکې**.
- One dose: perfective **وخورئ**; a routine: **هره ورځ يې خورئ**.
- Don't: **مه خورئ** (never مه وخورئ).
tip.pattern: ورځ کې دوه ځله + له ډوډۍ وروسته + وخورئ

new: ورځ کې دوه ځله، له ډوډۍ وروسته.

sentences.native: دا ګولۍ سهار او ماښام يوه يوه وخورئ.
sentences.roman: dā golə́y sahā́r aw māṣā́m yáwa yáwa wə́xwrəy.
sentences.en: Take one of these tablets morning and evening.

sentences.native: د ماشوم شربت هر اته ساعته ورکړئ.
sentences.roman: də māshúm sharbát har atə́ sāʿáta wárkṛəy.
sentences.en: Give the child's syrup every eight hours.

sentences.native: دا ملهم ورځ کې درې ځله په زخم ولګوئ.
sentences.roman: dā malhám wradz ke dre dzə́la pə zaxm wə́lagawəy.
sentences.en: Put this cream on the cut three times a day.

sentences.native: دوه دوه څاڅکي په غوږ کې واچوئ.
sentences.roman: dwa dwa tsā́tski pə ġwaẓ ke wā́chawəy.
sentences.en: Put two drops in the ear each time.

sentences.native: لومړی خوراک همدا اوس وخورئ.
sentences.roman: lumṛáy xwarā́k hamdā́ os wə́xwrəy.
sentences.en: Take the first dose right now.

sentences.native: تر هغه چې شربت خلاص شي، هره ورځ يې څښئ.
sentences.roman: tər haġə́ che sharbát xlās shi, hára wradz ye tsṣəy.
sentences.en: Keep taking the syrup every day until it's finished.

sentences.native: دا ګولۍ په خالي ګېډه مه خورئ.
sentences.roman: dā golə́y pə xālí géḍa ma xwrəy.
sentences.en: Don't take these tablets on an empty stomach.

sentences.native: له خوب مخکې يو خوراک شربت وڅښئ.
sentences.roman: la xob mə́xke yaw xwarā́k sharbát wə́tsṣəy.
sentences.en: Take a dose of syrup before bed.

sentences.native: له ډوډۍ مخکې که وروسته؟
sentences.roman: la ḍoḍə́y mə́xke ka wrústa?
sentences.en: Before or after food?

sentences.native: ورځ کې څو ځله يې وخورم؟
sentences.roman: wradz ke tso dzə́la ye wə́xwrəm?
sentences.en: How many times a day should I take it?

tip.title: Visiting someone who is ill
tip.body:
- Visiting the sick (**د ناروغ پوښتنه**) is a duty: go, bring fruit or juice, and keep it short.
- Say **خدای دې شفا درکړي** and **ژر جوړ شې**.
- Ask: **اوس څنګه يې؟ درملو اغېز وکړ؟** 'did the medicine work?' — درمل is the doer, so it's oblique: **درملو**.

sentences.native: درملو اغېز وکړ؟
sentences.roman: darmaló aġéz wə́kaṛ?
sentences.en: Did the medicine work?

sentences.native: ګولۍ اغېز نه کوي، تبه لا هم لرم.
sentences.roman: golə́y aġéz na kawí, tabə́ lā ham lárəm.
sentences.en: The tablets aren't working, I still have a fever.

sentences.native: ډاکټر ويلي چې له غوښې پرهېز وکړم.
sentences.roman: ḍākṭár wayə́li che la ġwáṣe parhéz wə́kṛəm.
sentences.en: The doctor's told me to stay off meat.

sentences.native: پرهېز کوې که نه؟
sentences.roman: parhéz kawé ka na?
sentences.en: Are you sticking to your diet or not?

sentences.native: شکر، اوس ډېر ښه يم.
sentences.roman: shukr, os ḍer ṣə yəm.
sentences.en: Thank God, I'm much better now.

sentences.native: ژر جوړ شې، وروره! ستا لپاره مې مڼې راوړې.
sentences.roman: zhər joṛ she, wróra! stā lapā́ra me maṇé rā́wṛe.
sentences.en: Get well soon, brother! I brought you some apples.

sentences.native: د ناروغ پوښتنې ته ځو.
sentences.roman: də nāróġ puṣtə́ne ta dzu.
sentences.en: We're going to visit someone who's ill.

sentences.native: که درمل اغېز ونه کړي، بيا ډاکټر ته لاړ شه.
sentences.roman: ka darmál aġéz wə́na kṛi, biyā́ ḍākṭár ta lāṛ sha.
sentences.en: If the medicine doesn't work, go back to the doctor.

sentences.native: تر هغه چې بشپړ روغ شې، کار ته مه ځه.
sentences.roman: tər haġə́ che bashpáṛ roġ she, kār ta ma dza.
sentences.en: Don't go to work until you're completely well.
